newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's President calls ministerial meeting on job.
newsitem.headline: Italy's President calls ministerial meeting on job.

text.p: Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro called for a conference on unemployment to be held at the presidential palace in Rome on Thursday afternoon.
Scalfaro, on a visit to the northeast town of Rovigo, said apart from himself, Prime Minister Romano Prodi and other ministers would also take part in the meeting.
"Unemployment is terrible, affecting the fundamental rights of the individual," Scalfaro said, adding that the "absolute commitment" of all was needed to resolve the dramatic situation.

He said he had called the top-level meeting because it was his job to keep himself informed. "The head of state is not putting himself in the place of the government, he just wants to be kept up to date on the situation."

Prodi, who has said tackling unemployment is a priority of his government, said two weeks ago that unemployment in Italy rose 0.4 percent in 1996. Latest official data put the national unemployment rate at 12.2 percent.
